subject: poppr.amova - "within variance" flag has no effect

messages.author: 1c20d3219b12ab48
messages.subject: poppr.amova - "within variance" flag has no effect
parts:
I found that the "within" argument in poppr.amova seems to have no effect.
Taking from the example in documentation:

#data preparation
library(poppr)
data(Aeut)
strata(Aeut) <- other(Aeut)$population_hierarchy[-1]
agc <- as.genclone(Aeut)

#amova, with and without "within individual" variance
amova.result.within <- poppr.amova(agc, ~Pop/Subpop, within = TRUE)
amova.result        <- poppr.amova(agc, ~Pop/Subpop, within = FALSE)

#comparing results
> all(amova.result.within$results == amova.result$results)
[1] TRUE
> all(amova.result.within$componentsofcovariance == amova.result$componentsofcovariance)
[1] TRUE
> all(amova.result.within$statphi == amova.result$statphi)
[1] TRUE

I would expect differences. In particular, even when within = FALSE, the variation within samples is computed, and takes a fraction of the total variance.

My software:
- poppr version : 2.1.1
- ade4 version : 1.7-4
- R version 3.2.3
- all run on my Ubuntu box

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: poppr.amova - "within variance" flag has no effect
parts:
'samples' in this case simply means the smallest unit of the population hierarchy. Notice that you specified a hierarchy of ~Pop/Subpop, but the results do not mention "Subpop" (while they do mention "Pop"). This is an unfortunate byproduct of how ade4 (which poppr uses for the underlying amova calculation) presents the results.

Take a look at what happens when you restrict the analysis to just between Pop:

library('poppr')
data(Aeut)
Aeut
## /// GENIND OBJECT /////////
## 
##  // 187 individuals; 56 loci; 56 alleles; size: 66.5 Kb
## 
##  // Basic content
##    @tab:  187 x 56 matrix of allele counts
##    @loc.n.all: number of alleles per locus (range: 56-56)
##    @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)
##    @type:  PA
##    @call: old2new_genind(object = x, donor = new(class(x)))
## 
##  // Optional content
##    @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 90-97)
##    @other: a list containing: population_hierarchy 
strata(Aeut) <- other(Aeut)$population_hierarchy[-1]
poppr.amova(Aeut, ~Pop/Subpop)
## 
##  No missing values detected.
## 
## $call
## ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)
## 
## $results
##                             Df    Sum Sq     Mean Sq
## Between Pop                  1 1051.2345 1051.234516
## Between samples Within Pop  16  273.4575   17.091091
## Within samples             169  576.5059    3.411277
## Total                      186 1901.1979   10.221494
## 
## $componentsofcovariance
##                                            Sigma          %
## Variations  Between Pop                11.063446  70.006786
## Variations  Between samples Within Pop  1.328667   8.407483
## Variations  Within samples              3.411277  21.585732
## Total variations                       15.803391 100.000000
## 
## $statphi
##                         Phi
## Phi-samples-total 0.7841427
## Phi-samples-Pop   0.2803128
## Phi-Pop-total     0.7000679
##
poppr.amova(Aeut, ~Pop)
## 
##  No missing values detected.
## 
## $call
## ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)
## 
## $results
##                  Df    Sum Sq     Mean Sq
## Between samples   1 1051.2345 1051.234516
## Within samples  185  849.9633    4.594396
## Total           186 1901.1979   10.221494
## 
## $componentsofcovariance
##                                 Sigma         %
## Variations  Between samples 11.209719  70.92911
## Variations  Within samples   4.594396  29.07089
## Total variations            15.804116 100.00000
## 
## $statphi
##                         Phi
## Phi-samples-total 0.7092911


Hope that helps,
Zhian

Hi Zhian, 
Thanks for helping me get started with poppr! I was wondering about this AMOVA test when you only use the single stratum "Pop" to split your dataset into populations. My understanding in the example you gave:

## Between samples   1 1051.2345 1051.234516
## Within samples  185  849.9633    4.594396
## Total           186 1901.1979   10.221494

...Is that "samples" should be read as "populations". 
However, in this tutorial (http://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/AMOVA.html)  they state, "This example was performed with a data set of dominant (AFLP) markers, but it can also be performed on codominant markers such as SNPs or SSRs. What I'm wondering is why, when I use a SSR dataset and set within=TRUE, do I still only get the same three levels (between samples, within samples, and total) and not another one for within individuals?

Thanks!
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: poppr.amova - "within variance" flag has no effect
parts:
He Melanie,

This is a good followup question. If you supply a diploid population with only one stratum, then you should have four rows in your results: Between Pop, Between samples, Within Samples, and Total. Here's an example with the nancycats data set:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))
data(nancycats)
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(Pop = pop(nancycats))
poppr.amova(nancycats, ~Pop, quiet = TRUE)

#> Warning in is.euclid(xdist): Zero distance(s)
#> Distance matrix is non-euclidean.
#> Utilizing quasieuclid correction method. See ?quasieuclid for details.
#> Warning in is.euclid(distmat): Zero distance(s)
#> $call
#> ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)
#> 
#> $results
#>                             Df    Sum Sq  Mean Sq
#> Between Pop                 16  141.6545 8.853408
#> Between samples Within Pop 220  611.9992 2.781815
#> Within samples             237  502.7677 2.121383
#> Total                      473 1256.4215 2.656282
#> 
#> $componentsofcovariance
#>                                            Sigma          %
#> Variations  Between Pop                0.2189376   8.198264
#> Variations  Between samples Within Pop 0.3302159  12.365154
#> Variations  Within samples             2.1213828  79.436582
#> Total variations                       2.6705364 100.000000
#> 
#> $statphi
#>                          Phi
#> Phi-samples-total 0.20563418
#> Phi-samples-Pop   0.13469412
#> Phi-Pop-total     0.08198264


In this case, the samples are the individuals since that's the lowest level of the hierarchy.

If you are getting only three levels, then that might be a bug in a corner case that I'm not aware of. If you can't reproduce the example above, then try updating poppr and/or R. If you still have the same problem, please post a reproducible example at https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues (if you don't have a github account, creating one is easy. If you don't want to create one, you can post the issue here, but I'm not sure how easily you'll be able to track it: https://gitreports.com/issue/grunwaldlab/poppr).  

Best,
Zhian

parts:
Hello Melanie,

It's not a "problem" per se, but within individual variances cannot be calculated this way. Instead, poppr will just quietly ignore within = TRUE. Here's an example with polyploid Phytophthora infestans data bundled with poppr:

library("poppr")
#> Loading required package: adegenet
#> Loading required package: ade4
#> 
#>    /// adegenet 2.0.2 is loaded ////////////
#> 
#>    > overview: '?adegenet'
#>    > tutorials/doc/questions: 'adegenetWeb()' 
#>    > bug reports/feature requests: adegenetIssues()
#> This is poppr version 2.3.0. To get started, type package?poppr
#> OMP parallel support: unavailable
data(Pinf)
Pinf  # polyploid data
#> 
#> This is a genclone object
#> -------------------------
#> Genotype information:
#> 
#>    72 multilocus genotypes 
#>    86 tetraploid individuals
#>    11 codominant loci
#> 
#> Population information:
#> 
#>     2 strata - Continent, Country
#>     2 populations defined - South America, North America
suppressWarnings(poppr.amova(Pinf, ~Continent, quiet = TRUE, within = TRUE))

#> Distance matrix is non-euclidean.
#> Utilizing quasieuclid correction method. See ?quasieuclid for details.

#> $call
#> ade4::amova(samples = xtab, distances = xdist, structures = xstruct)
#> 
#> $results
#>                 Df   Sum Sq  Mean Sq

#> Between samples  1  28.4403 28.44030
#> Within samples  84 331.0995  3.94166
#> Total           85 359.5398  4.22988

#> 
#> $componentsofcovariance
#>                                 Sigma         %

#> Variations  Between samples 0.5775447  12.77979
#> Variations  Within samples  3.9416602  87.22021
#> Total variations            4.5192050 100.00000

#> 
#> $statphi
#>                         Phi

#> Phi-samples-total 0.1277979

Hope that helps.
Zhian
